headline: Discussed Old Tower Hill Road Form-Based Code revisions and farm stand zoning rules without taking formal action.
summary: The Planning Board reviewed draft revisions to the Old Tower Hill Road Neighborhood Project Form-Based Code and discussed suggestions from legal counsel, with further review planned for the August 13, 2026 Work Session. The board also discussed zoning rules for farm stands, including the 5-acre minimum farm size, and directed Planning Department staff to research models from other New England towns.
plain_text:
Town of South Kingstown   
Planning Board   
Work Session Meeting Minutes 
Tuesday, July 21, 2026 at 6:30 PM   
South Kingstown Town Hall, Conference Room 
180 High Street, Wakefield, RI 02879 
www.southkingstownri.gov  
Maria H. Mack, Chair 
Susan Axelrod, Vice Chair 
Elizabeth Karp, Secretary 
Paul Jordan 
Robyn Pothier 
Kaiper Wilson 
Armand Monaco 
 
A. Call to Order & Roll Call: 
The meeting was held in the Town Council Chambers. 
 
Ms. Mack called the meeting to order at 6:35 p.m. 
 
ROLL CALL:   
Present:  Susan Axelrod, Liz Karp, Paul Jordan, Robyn Pothier, Kaiper Wilson, Armand Monaco, and Maria Mack. 
Absent:  None 
 
Also present:  James Rabbitt, Director of Planning; Brian Wagner, Deputy Director of Planning; Curtis Dufour, Principal 
Planner; and David Marks, Special Legal Counsel. 
B. Recommendations to Town Council: 
 1. Old Tower Hill Road Neighborhood Project, Form-Based Code: Review and Recommendation to the South 
Kingstown Town Council. 
Mr. Rabbitt reported that the Town Council requested the Planning Department work with legal counsel and go over 
and refine the draft document.  Also, that the Town Council is tentatively scheduled to have public hearings on the 
proposed revisions at their first meeting in September, potentially continuing any public meeting to their second 
meeting in September. 
Mr. Rabbitt then discussed suggestions made by Andy Tietz, Special Legal Counsel. 
 
Discussion ensued regarding the Form Based Code. 
 
Mr. Rabbitt encouraged the Planning Board Members to send any bullet items and/or suggestions to him; the 
information and changes will be reviewed at the August 13, 2026, Work Session. 
 2. Zoning Ordinance Regulation on Farmstands. 
Mr. Rabbitt gave an overview of what the Town Council has tasked the Planning Board, the Town's legal team, as well as 
the Planning Department. 
Mr. Rabbitt stated that the structural aspects of farms, farm stands, events, and accessory uses for farms, are very 
structured within the Town's existing regulations.  The current zoning ordinance states that a farm stand is allowed on a 
farm; a farm is 5 acres or more. 
 
Attorney Marks reviewed the State laws governing farms/farm stands, and how local zoning is then followed.  South 
Kingstown does not recognize a farm that is less than 5 acres, for purposes of putting a farm stand on it.   
 
Discussion ensued. 
The Planning Department staff is to look at examples around New England and put out a couple of different models with 
layered structure and scalability, for the Planning Board to react to.  
C. Reports and Special Items: None
D. Adjournment: 
Upon a Motion made by Ms. Wilson, duly seconded by Mr. Jordan, the meeting was adjourned at 8:00 p.m., by 
unanimous vote.
